findings.description: The release criteria are type-level only - "Existing field types, method signatures and union variant indices are compatibility acceptance criteria" with 0.1.1 preferred "if compatibility probes support it" - but the corrected parameter policy at lines 69-77 turns parameters the pinned spec no longer declares into validation errors before credentials and transport. That is a runtime behavior break no type-level probe can detect: AttackListOptions.search is a public field today and is sent on the wire via common::listing (crates/scm-sdk/src/airs/red_team/reports.rs:9, 51), while the pinned spec declares no search parameter for /v1/report/static/{job_id}/list-attacks (yaml:316-437). The fail-closed choice is the right one, but the version decision as written could land such a break in a patch release.
findings.required_fix: Require the per-parameter disposition ledger to feed the version decision: state that any parameter newly rejected before transport is a documented behavior break with a CHANGELOG entry, and that the 0.1.1-versus-0.2.0 choice must be justified against those runtime breaks rather than against type-level probes alone.

findings.description: The phase-9 entry now carries plan, scope_evidence, check_scope_rationale and limitations, but "reviews": [] is the only review bookkeeping: the preserved failed attempt (docs/reviews/phase-09-attempt-01.json, score 8.5, gate_passed false) and the dispositions of its seven findings are absent, unlike phases 2, 3, 6 and 8 which record review_attempts and review_fixes/review_advisories with resolution evidence. AGENTS.md:5 requires the review artifact, checks, limitations and outcome to be recorded in docs/phase-status.json, and the progress source of truth currently gives no trace that an earlier attempt failed or how it was answered.
findings.required_fix: Add "review_attempts": ["docs/reviews/phase-09-attempt-01.json"] to the phase-9 entry plus a review_fixes block mapping each attempt-01 finding (pin artifact, validation direction, parameter disposition, phase-9 command set, PHASES.md rows 9-12, FileFormat::Unknown, js-yaml) to its resolution evidence, noting the js-yaml item as partially deferred to Phase 10.

findings.description: The scoped command set exercises review, CI and evidence invariants plus the vendor pin, which is appropriate for a plan phase, but no executed credential or private-material scan covers the newly committed third-party file. test_auxiliary_evidence only unit-tests the scanner; the actual scan (scripts/check-private-material.py --check) runs solely in the phase-8 command set, so the one phase that adds 225 KB of new git-visible bytes records no executed scan over them. Risk is low because the file is a public upstream specification, but the check is inexpensive and already owned by the repository.
findings.required_fix: Add ["python", "scripts/check-private-material.py", "--check", "docs/checks/phase-09-private-material.json"] (or an equivalent scoped scan) to commands_for(9), rerun tools/check_phase.py --phase 9, and request a fresh review against the resulting source fingerprint.

evidence: docs/checks/phase-09.json:2-6 records phase 9, source_sha256 931c94d517bbd747988609fc265fb4d6cdabddb48025f1da08ea7f60f4bbe048 (equal to the reviewed hash in my prompt), source_unchanged true, passed true, checked_at 2026-10-18T11:17:55Z.

docs/checks/phase-09.json:9-155 contains exactly six executed checks, all exit_code 0 with retained streams: git diff --check; tools/verify-contracts.py (status verified, baseline 0.34.0, commit 4a80dbdb...); unittest test_vendor_red_team_plan.py (2 tests OK); test_review_phase.py (25 tests OK); test_ci.py (26 tests OK); test_auxiliary_evidence.py (32 tests OK). That list equals commands_for(9) at tools/check_phase.py:55-60 in the same order.

tools/review_phase.py:99-113 (check_evidence) requires phase, passed true, matching source_sha256, source_unchanged true and exact command-set equality with commands_for(phase) before any prompt is generated; tools/review_phase.py:205-219 is the verbatim template of the prompt I received, with the same source hash, so the recorded gate is bound to this exact source. tools/review_phase.py:43-60 excludes only docs/reviews/, docs/checks/ and docs/phase-status.json from the fingerprint, so the plan document and the vendor pin are inside the reviewed hash.

tools/test_vendor_red_team_plan.py:19-29 asserts commit afef9d08030a56e18a04ea078f589313f1fa2b0c, sha256 77f015de..., license MIT, commit-in-URL, non-symlink path, byte/hash equality with the committed file, and raises on a one-byte mutation; lines 31-49 run the pinned js-yaml (version equality against pin.yamlParser.version) over both the new and frozen specs and assert {version 0.93.0, openapi 3.1.0, operations 47, previous 36, added 11, removed [], parser 4.3.2}.

Independent path enumeration: contracts/vendor/red-team-data-plane/0.93.0/dp-openapi.yaml contains 46 path items (lines 44-2000) and contracts/sources/pan-dev/openapi-specs/prisma-airs-redteam/data-plane/dp-openapi.yaml contains 35 (lines 44-1556). The eleven differences are exactly the plan's table rows: /v1/scan/{job_id}/runtime-profile (yaml:219), /v1/report/static/{job_id}/asr (555), /v1/report/dynamic/{job_id}/asr (678), /v1/report/{job_id}/regenerate (976), /v1/report/{job_id}/status (1010), /v1/report/static/{job_id}/attack/{attack_id}/override (1076), .../attack-multi-turn/{attack_id}/override (1122), /v1/report/dynamic/{job_id}/stream/{stream_id}/override (1167), /v1/custom-attacks/job/{job_id}/attack/{attack_id}/override (1618), /v1/error-log/job/{job_id}/download (1716), /v2/report/{job_id}/download (1829). No old path is removed.

Per-route verification against the pinned bytes: PUT runtime-profile requires the body and returns JobResponseSchema (yaml:243-255) with RuntimeProfileUpdateRequestSchema closed and runtime_profile_id required at minLength 1/maxLength 256 (yaml:5298-5311); regenerate declares 202 RegenerateResponse and documents the 409 dedup (yaml:981-1003); ReportStatusResponse requires report_state over the closed ACTIVE/STALE/GENERATING/FAILED enum (yaml:5231-5256); ThreatOverrideRequest is additionalProperties:false with minItems 1/maxItems 100 and ThreatOverrideItem requires output_id (uuid) and nullable threat_override (yaml:7217-7252); AsrResponseSchema requires job_id/job_type/asr with asr bounded 0-100 (yaml:2190-2206); the error-log download 200 has no content block (yaml:1732-1734); /v2 download requires file_format referencing FileFormat (CSV/JSON/ALL) and returns ReportDownloadSchema (yaml:1867-1881, 4034-4041).

Compatibility-overlay verification: audio_technique appears in a required list only at yaml:2448 (AttackDetailResponseSchema) and yaml:2775 (AttackMultiTurnDetailResponseSchema) and is absent from the frozen 0.7.75 spec entirely; judge_reasoning is required only at yaml:2881 (AttackMultiTurnOutputResponseSchema) and yaml:2972 (AttackOutputResponseSchema) and is optional at yaml:3435, 6143, 6294. Other required-list hits for the plan's enumerated new fields belong to new schemas (audio_name in AttackAudioSchema yaml:2281; error_count in JobRuntimeMetricsSchema yaml:4668) or were already required in 0.7.75 (categories/target_type at frozen lines 3153-3155 and 4503-4504), so the four named waivers are the only newly required fields on pre-existing schemas that this scan reaches.

Plan-versus-code claims hold: RemediationDetail has no categories field and flattens unknown keys into extensions (crates/scm-sdk/src/models/generated.rs:159527-159542), matching plan:96-98; the parameter-disposition policy has concrete targets, e.g. AttackListOptions.search (crates/scm-sdk/src/airs/red_team/reports.rs:9) is sent through common::listing (reports.rs:51) although the pinned spec declares no search parameter for list-attacks (yaml:316-437); the 36 existing operations have real native methods across the named families (facade.rs:147, 165, 190, 230, 248, 263, 288, 305 and reports.rs:321 cover goal-categories, dashboard, error-log, languages, sentiment and generate-partial-report).

Attempt-01 dispositions verified in the current source: machine-readable pin and committed bytes now exist with a Phase 10 byte/hash/recount gate (plan:23-26, 167); validation direction is resolved explicitly for requests and responses with the named waivers and required tests (plan:119-130); the blanket silent-omission rule is replaced by pre-transport rejection, per-parameter negative tests and CHANGELOG entries (plan:69-77); the phase-9 command set is extended and was actually executed (check_phase.py:55-60 plus the recorded report); PHASES.md now carries rows and milestone records for phases 9-12 (docs/PHASES.md:19-22, 38-41, 54-62); FileFormat::Unknown rejection before credentials is stated and made a verification item (plan:141, 197); the phase-9 status entry carries scope_evidence, rationale and limitations (docs/phase-status.json:1805-1817).

Governance norm for redistributed vendor bytes, for comparison with the new pin: contracts/manifest.json:1845-1858 records path, repository, commit, upstreamPath, sourceUrl, license id, redistributed, usedForGeneration, sha256, gitBlobSha1 and bytes for the frozen copy of the same upstream file, with the notice text at contracts/licenses/pan-dev-e2e6e63e6acd.LICENSE:1-3 (MIT, Copyright (c) 2021 Palo Alto Networks). contracts/vendor/ contains only dp-openapi.yaml and source.json, and source.json:11 carries license "MIT" with no notice reference.
limitations: Only Read/Glob/Grep were available, so I could not recompute any hash: the 225109-byte length, sha256 77f015de..., gitBlobSha1 f9761d0a... and the prompt's check-report hash 85cc262e... are taken from the recorded artifacts and from tools/test_vendor_red_team_plan.py's passing in-gate comparison, not from independent computation. I also could not run git, so the claim that the working-tree change set is docs/governance plus the vendor pin rests on the git status snapshot, the passing contract-corpus set-equality check and my own reading.

Network access is prohibited, so I could not confirm that the committed bytes are what pan.dev revision afef9d08030a56e18a04ea078f589313f1fa2b0c actually serves. Source identity is verified only as internally self-consistent (file equals recorded hash, recount equals the recorded expectation) plus independently re-checkable later via the recorded sourceUrl, commit and gitBlobSha1.

My newly-required-field diff was targeted, not exhaustive: I compared required-list entries for the field names the plan enumerates plus the four named waivers across roughly 130 schemas, so a pre-existing optional field under a name outside that candidate set could in principle have become required without my noticing. The plan delegates the exhaustive machine diff to Phase 10 with a fail-closed rule.

Only the six recorded commands were executed for this source. No Rust compilation, test, generation-reproducibility, packaging, export-probe, dependency or live check ran in this phase, and the phase 1-8 reports are historical records bound to earlier fingerprints; I did not re-execute them. No canonical JSON conversion, schema closure diff or 47-row operation ledger exists yet, by design.

The 36-existing-operations-to-native-methods mapping is spot-checked across families rather than enumerated; the authoritative ledger is Phase 10 scope. Likewise I judged only Phase 9's acceptance criteria (source identity, scoped governance checks, settled new/existing contract, compatibility, security and verification policy) and did not score phases 10-12 deliverables.
Per the prompt I read no credential or tenant-registration material and stayed inside the repository; I did not rely on anything under .local/.
